title: Wealth, Credit & Controls
intro: This level covers client onboarding and classification, suitability and appropriateness, investment limits, trading restrictions and approvals. It also covers Lombard collateral valuation, margin calls, and the matrix maths used for portfolio risk.

key_concepts: Static data: name, address, tax residency, signatories, powers of attorney, standing instructions
Four-eyes and customer authentication for changes

modules.title: Trading Restrictions
modules.hook: Watch and restricted lists, insider information and MAR obligations, pre-trade blocking, and the handling of orders already in flight.

units.title: The restriction landscape
objectives: Learner can name the four sources of a trading restriction (law, firm policy, client instruction, instrument/market) and give one example each
Learner can distinguish restricted list, watch list and grey list by who sees it, what it blocks and when an instrument moves between them

key_concepts: legal, firm, client and instrument restrictions
restricted vs watch vs grey list
effect on order intake and no-tipping-off
time and scope of a restriction
blocked-security flag checked at order entry
units.worked_example: An order arrives for 20,000 shares of Alfa SpA (about EUR 310k at EUR 15.50), which sits on the restricted list because the bank advises on a pending bid: the order system blocks it, logs the attempt with timestamp and user, alerts compliance and gives the client a neutral message ('unable to accept'). The same order on the watch list would be accepted but flagged for surveillance.

units.worked_example: A treasury analyst hears on 3 March that Beta plc will launch a EUR 2bn bid at a 30% premium on 12 March: the fact is precise, non-public and price-sensitive, so trading Beta shares, advising others to do so or passing the news beyond need-to-know is prohibited. If Beta reports half-year results on 28 July, its PDMRs may not trade from 28 June to 28 July (30 calendar days before).

A user who can both create and release payments breaches SoD, so one right is removed or a compensating review is documented.

modules.title: Lombard Lending
modules.hook: Lombard loans, lending values and haircuts by asset class, concentration treatment, and the credit decision on a pledged portfolio.

units.title: What a Lombard loan is
objectives: Learner can describe a Lombard loan: borrower, pledged portfolio, credit line, bank rights
Learner can compute LTV (loan / market value) and lending-value utilisation (loan / lending value)
Learner can compute headroom from a lending value
Learner can name three use cases and three client risks
units.worked_example: A client pledges a EUR 2m portfolio for a EUR 800k credit line: LTV is 800/2,000 = 40%. If the portfolio's lending value is 60% of market value (EUR 1.2m), headroom is 1,200 - 800 = EUR 400k and utilisation is 66.7%. The bank cannot lend more than the lending value, however low the LTV looks.

exercises.task: LTV from loan and portfolio
Headroom from lending value
exercises.params: market value, average lending %, drawn amount

exercises.task: Identify the structure

units.title: Lending values and haircuts by asset class
objectives: Learner can assign lending values to assets by class using a haircut table (lending value = 1 - haircut)
Learner can compute total lending value, headroom and utilisation for a mixed pool
Learner can decide whether an asset is eligible at all (0% lending value)
Learner can rank two assets by haircut and explain why (liquidity, volatility, issuer, FX)
key_concepts: asset classes: IG bonds, blue-chip equities, funds, structured products, unlisted
Basel CRE22 supervisory haircuts as benchmark
units.worked_example: Pool of EUR 500k: EUR 280k IG bonds at 70% = 196k; EUR 170k blue-chip equities at 50% = 85k; EUR 50k unlisted fund units at 0% = 0. Lending value 281k. With EUR 280k drawn, headroom is only EUR 1k and utilisation 99.6%: a small fall triggers a call. Reference for a benchmark: Basel CRE22 uses 15% for main-index equities and 0.5/2/4% for AAA-AA sovereigns by maturity bucket.

exercises.task: Compute lending value per holding and total
exercises.params: holdings with market value and haircut %

exercises.task: Headroom and utilisation
Eligible vs ineligible assets
exercises.params: asset pool: listed equity, unlisted fund, private equity stake, crypto, listed bond

exercises.task: Which asset has the higher haircut?

units.title: Concentration, liquidity and stress
objectives: Learner can apply a concentration add-on to a single-name holding and recompute lending value
Learner can stress a pool by a market shock and compute stressed lending value and utilisation
Learner can spot wrong-way risk (pledged shares of the borrower's own company or a related issuer)
Learner can identify weaknesses in a lending policy document
key_concepts: CRR large exposures as the bank-side limit
units.worked_example: A EUR 1m pool: EUR 600k in one blue-chip stock (50% lending value less a 15-point add-on = 35% -> 210k) and EUR 400k IG bonds at 70% (280k): lending value 490k. With a EUR 400k loan, utilisation is 81.6%. A -35% shock on the stock cuts it to 390k and its lending value to 136.5k; total lending value 416.5k, utilisation 96.0%, and LTV on the stressed market value (790k) is 50.6%.

exercises.task: Lending value after concentration add-on

units.title: Pledge and collateral agreements

key_concepts: scope and substitution of pledged assets
units.worked_example: On default with EUR 800k principal, EUR 12k accrued interest and EUR 3k costs, the bank sells pledged securities of EUR 900k market value at a 2% realisation shortfall (EUR 882k): after EUR 815k of claims, EUR 67k surplus goes back to the client. If the agreement requires 3 business days' notice before realisation, the sale cannot start earlier unless the agreement allows immediate sale.

units.worked_example: A EUR 300k nominal barrier reverse convertible quoted at 96.0 bid has market value EUR 288k; its lending value is 30%, i.e. EUR 86.4k. When the underlying trades 5% above the barrier, policy cuts lending value to 0% for notes within 10% of the barrier: collateral falls by EUR 86.4k and a pool drawn near its limit is short by that amount.

units.title: Pricing, covenants and reviews
objectives: Learner can compute interest and fees with an Act/360 day count
Learner can test a facility against covenants and review dates
Learner can compute a Basel CRE22 comprehensive-approach exposure after collateral (simplified)
key_concepts: regulatory capital: E* = max(0, E x (1+He) - C x (1-Hc-Hfx))
units.worked_example: A EUR 800k loan at 3M EURIBOR + 1.25% (total 4.0%) costs EUR 32,000 a year, or 800k x 4% x 92/360 = EUR 8,177.78 for a 92-day quarter. A EUR 1m limit with 0.50% commitment fee on the EUR 200k undrawn adds EUR 1,000 a year. A covenant requires collateral of at least 125% of the loan (EUR 1.0m). For capital: EUR 800k exposure vs EUR 1m equities with 15% haircut and 8% FX mismatch gives E* = 800 - 1,000 x (1 - 0.15 - 0.08) = EUR 30k (holding-period scaling ignored).

units.title: Lombard credit approval and limit exceptions
objectives: Take a request from credit memo to limit set-up: purpose, collateral, lending value, requested limit, approval level
Decide which authority approves a temporary excess or a collateral exception from an authority table

key_concepts: Credit memo: client, purpose, collateral list, lending value, concentration, stress
Limit set-up in the credit system and linkage to collateral accounts
Credit committee and delegated credit authority by amount
Temporary excess vs permanent increase; maximum amount and duration
Collateral exceptions: concentrated position, illiquid asset, structured product at higher lending value
Conditions precedent, covenants and review cycle; lending values are illustrative bank practice
units.worked_example: A client pledges EUR 2.0m of diversified securities with an illustrative lending value of 60%, so EUR 1.2m. The approved limit is EUR 1.0m, fully drawn. The client asks for EUR 1.1m for 10 days: the EUR 100k temporary excess is 10% of the limit; an illustrative authority table lets the credit officer approve up to 10% for 30 days, and collateral still covers it (EUR 1.1m is below EUR 1.2m). A request to accept a single stock at 40% lending value instead of 20% is a collateral exception and goes to the credit committee.

modules.title: Margin & Margin Calls
modules.hook: Margin thresholds, margin call calculation and notification, deadlines, forced liquidation, and the handling of a market gap.

units.title: Margin basics
objectives: Learner can define initial margin, maintenance margin and equity
Learner can compute equity, leverage and margin ratio after a price move
Learner can compute the price at which a maintenance call occurs
Learner can describe the effect of leverage on returns
units.worked_example: A client buys EUR 100k of shares with EUR 50k own cash and EUR 50k borrowed: equity 50k, leverage 2x. A 20% fall leaves market value 80k, equity 30k and margin ratio 37.5%, with a loss of 20k = -40% on equity. With a 25% maintenance ratio, a call occurs when loan / (1 - 25%) = 50/0.75 = EUR 66.7k, a 33.3% fall.

exercises.task: Equity and margin ratio
Margin call price
Return on equity at leverage
Identify the term
Match terms to definitions

units.title: Reg T and FINRA 4210
objectives: Learner can apply Reg T initial margin (50%) and FINRA 4210 maintenance (25% long, 30% short) to a position
Learner can compute Reg T excess equity and buying power
Learner can decide whether a call is due from a position table
Learner can compute margin for a short sale
units.worked_example: A client buys USD 40,000 of stock with USD 20,000 cash; maintenance is 25%, so the stock can fall to about USD 26,700 before a call (loan 20,000 / 0.75). An account with market value USD 100k and loan USD 40k has equity 60k against the Reg T 50% requirement of 50k: excess 10k, buying power 20k. A USD 30,000 short needs 50% initial (15k on top of proceeds) and 30% maintenance (USD 9,000).

exercises.task: Requirement and excess
Buying power

units.title: The margin call process
objectives: Learner can run the call process from breach to cure or liquidation, with deadlines
Learner can compute the shortfall and the cure amount by top-up and by sell-down
Learner can decide on liquidation timing for a case
Learner can place deadlines on a timeline from the margin agreement
units.worked_example: After a 15% fall in the equities of the K1.2 pool (170k -> 144.5k), lending value is 196 + 72.25 = EUR 268.25k against a EUR 280k loan: shortfall EUR 11.75k. Cure options: pledge EUR 11.75k cash (100% lending value); repay EUR 11.75k; or sell EUR 23.5k of equity and repay the loan (S = 11.75 / (1 - 0.5)), after which loan 256.5k equals lending value 60.5k + 196k. If there is no response by the deadline (e.g. T+2 12:00) the bank can sell.

exercises.task: Order the steps of a margin call

units.title: Portfolio margin and risk-based
objectives: Learner can describe portfolio margin versus strategy-based margin
Learner can compute a portfolio-margin requirement as the worst loss over a scenario grid
Learner can state eligibility and risk limits of portfolio margin
Learner can name CCP-style risk-based margin (SPAN/TIMS, EMIR confidence levels)
units.worked_example: A client holds 5,000 shares at USD 100 and 50 protective put contracts (strike 90, bought at USD 4). Revalue at -15%, -10%, -5%, 0, +5%, +10% and +15% (intrinsic put values): P&L = 5,000 x (S - 100) + 5,000 x (max(90 - S, 0) - 4). Worst loss is -USD 70,000 at S = 85 (and at 90), so portfolio margin is USD 70,000, against USD 250,000 (50% of 500k) under Reg T.

units.worked_example: On a EUR 50m derivatives portfolio with daily VM, a EUR 1.2m mark-to-market move triggers a call for EUR 1.2m (no threshold, MTA EUR 500k exceeded) delivered the next morning; in government bonds with a 2% haircut the bank delivers 1.2 / 0.98 = EUR 1,224,490 market value. In a 7-day repo of EUR 10m bonds at a 2% haircut the cash lent is EUR 9.8m; at 2.5% Act/360 the interest is 9.8m x 2.5% x 7/360 = EUR 4,763.89.

modules.title: Linear Algebra
modules.hook: Vectors, matrices, matrix products and inverses, and their use in portfolio variance and covariance across several assets.

units.title: Vectors and portfolio weights
objectives: Learner can add vectors and multiply a vector by a scalar, including a leverage scale-up
Learner can compute a dot product to get portfolio return from weights and expected returns
Learner can convert EUR holdings to a weight vector that sums to 1
Learner can compute a vector's length (norm) and state when two vectors are orthogonal
units.worked_example: Weights (0.5, 0.3, 0.2) and expected returns (6%, 4%, 10%): w . r = 0.03 + 0.012 + 0.02 = 6.2%. From EUR holdings (250k, 150k, 100k) the weights are holdings / 500k = (0.5, 0.3, 0.2). Scaling the weights by 1.5 gives (0.75, 0.45, 0.30), a 150% gross exposure financed by a 50% loan, and return 1.5 x 6.2% = 9.3% before interest.

exercises.task: Dot product of weights and returns

units.title: Matrices and operations
objectives: Learner can multiply two 2x2 matrices and a 2x2 matrix by a 2x1 vector
Learner can state when a product is defined from the dimensions
Learner can transpose a vector or matrix and recognise a symmetric matrix
Learner can use the identity matrix
key_concepts: dimension rule (m x n)(n x p)
units.worked_example: [[1,2],[3,4]] x [[0,1],[1,0]] = [[2,1],[4,3]] (multiplying by a swap matrix swaps columns). Covariance matrix [[0.04, 0.006],[0.006, 0.01]] times weights (0.5, 0.5) gives (0.023, 0.008), the first step of portfolio variance. A 2x1 times 2x1 product is undefined: the shapes do not match.

units.title: Covariance matrices
objectives: Learner can compute a covariance from volatilities and correlation, and the reverse
Learner can compute a sample covariance from a short return series
Learner can build a 2x2 and 3x3 covariance matrix

units.worked_example: Volatilities 20% and 10% with correlation 0.3: covariance 0.3 x 0.2 x 0.1 = 0.006; matrix [[0.04, 0.006],[0.006, 0.01]]. From returns X = (2, -1, 3, 0)% and Y = (1, 0, 2, 1)%: means 1 and 1, products of deviations (0, 2, 2, 0) sum 4, sample covariance 4 / 3 = 1.33 %^2. The matrix [[0.04, 0.05],[0.05, 0.01]] implies correlation 2.5, so it is invalid.

exercises.task: Covariance from volatilities and correlation

units.title: Portfolio variance as w'Σw
objectives: Learner can compute portfolio variance as w'Sigma w for 2 and 3 assets
Learner can compute the minimum-variance weights for two assets
Learner can compare portfolio volatility with the weighted average volatility
Learner can explain diversification as a consequence of correlation below 1
key_concepts: min-variance weight w1 = (s2^2 - s12)/(s1^2 + s2^2 - 2 s12)
units.worked_example: With the Q6.4 assets at 50/50: variance = 0.25 x 0.04 + 0.25 x 0.01 + 2 x 0.25 x 0.006 = 0.0155, volatility 12.45%, against a weighted average of 15%. Minimum variance: w1 = (0.01 - 0.006)/(0.04 + 0.01 - 0.012) = 10.5% in the 20%-vol asset, 89.5% in the other, variance 0.00958 (vol 9.79%), below either asset alone.

exercises.task: Portfolio variance for two assets

units.title: Eigenvalues and principal components
objectives: Learner can find the eigenvalues of a 2x2 covariance matrix from trace and determinant
Learner can find the direction (eigenvector) of the largest eigenvalue
Learner can compute the share of variance explained by each component
Learner can interpret PCA factors of a yield curve (level, slope, curvature)
units.worked_example: For [[0.04, 0.006],[0.006, 0.01]]: trace 0.05, determinant 0.000364, eigenvalues (0.05 +/- sqrt(0.0025 - 0.001456))/2 = 0.04116 and 0.00884. The first component explains 0.04116 / 0.05 = 82.3% of variance with direction about (0.98, 0.19), mostly the 20%-vol asset. In yield-curve PCA the first three components typically explain the vast majority of variation (level, slope, curvature).

exercises.task: Eigenvalues of a 2x2 matrix

units.title: Consolidation: risk of a Lombard pool
objectives: Learner can build a 3x3 covariance matrix and compute pool volatility with w'Sigma w
Learner can convert annual volatility to a 1-day 99% loss in EUR
Learner can compare the loss figure with weighted-average risk and with lending haircuts
Learner can explain why haircuts exceed 1-day VaR (liquidation period, stress, gaps)
units.worked_example: Pool EUR 1m: equities 40% (vol 20%), equity fund 20% (15%), IG bonds 40% (5%), correlations 0.8, 0.1, 0.2. Variance = 0.0121, vol 11.0%, below the 13% weighted average. 1-day 99% loss = 11.0% / sqrt(252) x 2.326 x 1m = EUR 16.1k (undiversified: EUR 19.1k); 10-day 51k. Haircuts of 50%, 40%, 30% give a EUR 400k cushion, far above VaR because they cover stressed gaps and a 20-day liquidation.
